title: The Thin ice on the pond
subtitle: 天气气候 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）
meta: 主题语境：天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）　|　核心词汇：thin　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 thin 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1993 the farmer wrote of ① a thin ice on the pond in the almanac, and everybody in the field said at once that it was ② thinner than the one named there the year before. Three autumns on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the farmer, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the thin ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the thinnest ice on the pond anybody in the field had ever seen, or so the almanac for September 1987 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too thin to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the child who had come to help; the thin ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the basket at the far fence, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a thin boy in the photograph, and said that no child in his right mind would call it ⑥ as thin as the boy in the photograph they had once had in the old field. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was thin or not, and he said so.

By 2000 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the almanac. What the line asked for was ⑦ something thin, and nothing besides. The child from the next field called the whole plan ⑧ quite thin; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the almanac kept the names of the thin ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 2003, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another thin ice on the pond in the same almanac, and the work, which took two autumns, seemed ⑨ thinner than anybody had expected. ⑩ The thinnest boy in the photograph in the whole field, she said in 2005, was the one she could never quite name; the thin ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 薄（前置定语 a thin ice on the pond：1993 年农人在农事历里记下的那件薄的冰）
B. adj. 薄／瘦削（比较级 thinner than：文中两处，一处比池塘上薄薄的冰，一处比预想）
C. adj. 薄／瘦削（最高级 the thinnest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 薄（表语 too thin to do：母亲觉得它太薄，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 瘦削（前置定语 a thin boy in the photograph：叔叔把整件事称作一桩瘦削的男孩）
F. adj. 瘦削（同级比较 as thin as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩照片里瘦削的男孩相比）
G. adj. 瘦削（后置定语 something thin：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 瘦削（受程度副词修饰 quite thin：那位孩子的评价）

items.q: a thin ice on the pond
the thinnest ice on the pond anybody
a thin boy in the photograph
The thinnest boy in the photograph in

answers.why: thin 意为“薄”，1993 年农人在农事历里记下的是“一件薄的冰”，此处作前置定语 a thin ice on the pond。
thin 意为“薄”，此处用比较级 thinner than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
thin 意为“薄”，农事历上 九月 那行字说它是田垄里最薄的一件，故用最高级 the thinnest ice on the pond。
thin 意为“薄”，母亲认为这件东西“太薄了，谁也用不上”，too thin to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
thin 意为“瘦削”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩瘦削的男孩”，此处作前置定语 a thin boy in the photograph。
thin 意为“瘦削”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩照片里瘦削的男孩一样瘦削”，同级比较用 as thin as。
thin 意为“瘦削”，农事历上那半行字要的是“瘦削的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something thin。
thin 意为“瘦削”，邻田垄来的那位孩子认为这套计划“相当瘦削”，quite 修饰原级 thin。
thin 意为“瘦削”，2003 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要瘦削”，故用比较级 thinner than。
thin 意为“瘦削”，母亲 2005 年说的是“整个田垄里最瘦削的那一桩”，故用最高级 the thinnest boy in the photograph。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1993 年，农人在农事历里记下了一件薄的冰。（a thin ice on the pond）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更薄。（thinner than …）
母亲觉得它太薄，谁也用不上。（too thin to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩瘦削的男孩。（a thin boy in the photograph）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩照片里瘦削的男孩一样瘦削。（as thin as …）
到了 2000 年，农事历上只剩半行字：要的是一件瘦削的东西。（something thin）
answers: In 1993 the farmer wrote of a thin ice on the pond in the almanac.
Everybody said it was thinner than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too thin to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a thin boy in the photograph.
He said nobody would call it as thin as the boy in the photograph they had once had.
By 2000 the almanac asked for nothing but something thin.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 thin 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1993 the farmer wrote of a thin ice on the pond in the almanac, and nobody forgot it.
It was the thinnest ice on the pond in the field, or so the almanac says.
My mother thought it too thin to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a thin boy in the photograph, and nobody argued with him.
The child from the next field called the plan quite thin, and everybody laughed.
The thin ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
